headline: Medium risk: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/file-facing finance workflows can feed unverified outputs into a non-runnable Spring Integration sample, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct data-leak path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and uses a “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern, so attacker-controlled content can plausibly enter its outputs. spring-integration-samples is a Spring Integration sample repo, which commonly acts as a message-processing bridge; even though it is not runnable here, the pairwise pathway is plausible and not blocked by any cited isolation mechanism.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests untrusted MCP or API content and emits it into a Spring Integration flow
IF the Spring sample is adapted into a live message bridge without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow
Add explicit provenance tags to all OpenBB outputs
Reject instruction-like text in downstream Spring handlers
Run the pair in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, but its network egress is none and the B profile shows no data classes touched or outbound surfaces. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, a direct leakage route from A to B is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to accidental local exposure if operators manually move files.
conditions: IF operators manually copy sensitive OpenBB outputs into the Spring sample workspace
IF a shared filesystem is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep sensitive OpenBB exports in a separate directory
Avoid copying financial data into sample projects
Use redacted test fixtures only
Verify no shared cloud sync is enabled
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple instances, while spring-integration-samples is not runnable and shows no write or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping write surface, git mutation, or shared mutable resource, so a real capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because the B profile is sparse.
conditions: IF the Spring samples are converted into a writable service that shares state with OpenBB
IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or OAuth scope
mitigations: Keep B as read-only sample code
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Run only one writer per resource
Document ownership of any shared state
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit finance-related outputs through APIs/MCP, and Spring Integration samples are designed to route messages, so B could treat A’s output as input without verification if adapted into a live flow. Because B is not runnable in the profile, the pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, but the interaction is still plausible enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF B is used as a live integration pipeline that consumes OpenBB outputs
IF downstream handlers trust A’s outputs without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step before B consumes A output
Require human review for finance-derived facts
Log source provenance alongside each message
Use schema checks on all exchanged payloads
requires-engineering: add automated verification against primary sources

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, which can carry retention and redistribution obligations. The B profile has no compliance metadata, so no direct mismatch is proven; however, the absence of residency/retention controls on B means the safest reading is a potential policy mismatch if A’s regulated data is routed into B.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data from OpenBB is routed into the Spring sample
IF B stores, logs, or republishes that data without matching retention rules
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into B
Strip secrets and licensed fields before export
Set short log retention on any shared pipeline
Review data-handling notices for OpenBB outputs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
